hits.title: Dynatrace to acquire Arize in $915M AI observability deal
hits.snippet: Dynatrace has agreed to acquire AI observability company Arize in a cash and stock transaction valued at $915 million, bringing AI evaluation and production observability under the same platform. The deal is expected to close later this quarter or early in Dynatrace’s third quarter, subject to regulatory approval and other closing conditions.Arize focuses on monitoring and evaluating AI models, applications and agents, including detecting hallucinations, measuring output quality and tracing how AI systems behave. Dynatrace plans to connect those capabilities with its existing visibility into applications, infrastructure, GPU usage and business processes. That would give teams a way to follow an AI application from testing and evaluation through deployment and ongoing production [...] Mergers and Acquisitions, AI/ML # Dynatrace to acquire Arize in $915M AI observability deal By MSSP Alert Team

hits.title: Dynatrace acquires observability firm Arize in $915m deal
hits.snippet: (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook X Linkedin Bluesky Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Subscribe to our newsletter Dynatrace has agreed to acquire observability specialist Arize for $915 million, as the vendor looks to expand its capabilities across the AI development lifecycle. The deal will bring together Arize’s AI evaluation technology with Dynatrace’s production monitoring capabilities, enabling customers to evaluate, operate, and continuously improve AI applications. AI observability has become increasingly important as businesses move AI applications into production, connecting model and agent behaviour with application performance, GPU utilization, infrastructure health, and business processes.

hits.title: Arize AI acquires Velvet to expand support for AI observability, LLM evaluation - SiliconANGLE
hits.snippet: Velvet started in 2023 from a more developer-centric perspective as an observability platform for AI aimed at assisting engineers working with logs produced by models from Anthropic PBC and OpenAI. The big takeaway for the company is that it allows developers to get set up and running with model comparison, analysis and evaluation in under five minutes. The company now provides an AI gateway to capture traces, an AI SQL editor for analytics and evaluation tooling for experiments and monitoring. [...] Chris Hendel, Velvet’s co-founder and chief technology officer, will lead platform engineering initiatives at Arize. These include guiding and focusing on developer experience initiatives and accelerating the adoption of the company’s enterprise Arize AX model evaluation and observability platform, its open-source AI observability platform Phoenix OSS and the company’s Arize AI Copilot. The companies did not disclose the terms of the deal. Emma Lawler, founder and former CEO of Velvet, told SiliconANGLE that she was impressed by Arize’s team’s deep background in the business and how quickly they handled each new phase of AI. hits.title: Dynatrace Acquires Arize for $915M | Larry Dignan posted on the topic | LinkedIn
hits.snippet: Every so often, an acquisition quietly marks the moment two industries become one. This is one of them. Dynatrace has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Arize AI, the company that essentially created the AI observability category six years ago. Terms weren't disclosed. Here's the shift worth understanding. For a decade, "observability" meant watching your software: the logs and traces that tell you why a system broke. Then AI arrived, and a separate discipline appeared: watching your models and agents, why they answered, why they drifted, where they failed. Two markets, two toolsets. [...] The AI agent observability space is taking off — but how can enterprises be sure what observability products and solutions they need? Observability startup groudcover (lower case "g" intentional) announced this week that it raised $100 million in a round led by One Peak, bringing its total funding to $160 million. The company says it has more than 250 paying customers, tripled annual recurring revenue over the past year and is increasingly replacing established observability platforms inside enterprise environments.
